The menu has a wide variety of options and we decided to split the Arizona Cobb salad and the French dip. Both meals arrived and were split for both of us, nice touch!  The salad was great with a southwestern, avocados, black beans and corn over romaine with a tasty Mexican dressing. The trip French dip had a great mayo sauce and hot au jus, the only thing was it could have better bread than the white loaf they served. Overall a great meal.

reviews.text:
We celebrated my mother-in-law’s 80th birthday at the Tavern at The Phoenician, and I can honestly say it was the most magical evening we could have imagined.

From the moment we arrived, the team had our party table set up perfectly. Every detail was thoughtfully handled, and they went above and beyond to make her feel celebrated and special all night long. It wasn’t just service, it was care.

The food was exceptional. Every dish was beautifully prepared and delicious. But what truly elevated the evening was the dueling piano performance. The artists were incredibly talented, wildly entertaining, and knew exactly how to read the room. They created an atmosphere that was electric and joyful.

My mother-in-law was brought to tears more than once. She sang. She danced. She clapped in pure, childlike joy all evening long. It was, without question, the best birthday party she has ever had.

Even the other patrons contributed to the magic. The room felt celebratory, warm, and alive. You cannot manufacture that kind of energy, but somehow this place does.

If you are looking for a venue that delivers not just a dinner, but an unforgettable experience, this is it.

Thank you for giving our family a night we will never forget.

With the awesome staff at the Phoenician, I know you can throw together a better buffet experience. Last night’s meal just makes my family and me miss the holiday buffet that the Ritz Carlton used to have.

reviews.text:
We celebrated Christmas Day dinner at The Phoenician Tavern and had a truly wonderful experience. From the moment we arrived, the service stood out — friendly, welcoming, and incredibly accommodating, which immediately set the tone for a relaxed and enjoyable evening.

The property itself is stunning. The resort is beautifully maintained, and our window seating offered gorgeous views overlooking the golf course, adding a peaceful and festive atmosphere to the night. It felt special without being stuffy — exactly what you want on Christmas.

The buffet was excellent, with a great variety of well-prepared dishes that felt thoughtful and elevated rather than overwhelming. Everything we tried was fresh, flavorful, and satisfying. The dessert selection was equally impressive and the perfect way to end the meal.

Overall, The Phoenician Tavern delivered a memorable Christmas experience — beautiful setting, attentive service, and a solid, delicious spread of food and desserts. We left feeling happy, full, and already looking forward to coming back. Highly recommend for a holiday meal or special occasion.

reviews.text: We have dined at the Phoenician before and it was absolutely phenomenal but it was our first Christmas Buffet at the Phoenician Tavern! I thought this would be high end, and a Christmas night dinner to remember/ possibly make a tradition. BUT to charge $85 plus the service fee and the 20% tip (because what kind of scrooge wouldn’t tip on Christmas Day) this is NOT worth it.. $300 later and I’ve never been more disappointed in a restaurant that claims to be resort style.. I have also NEVER written a review, specially a negative one like this but hopefully it saves someone else a horrible Christmas night..The $22 drink I had tasted like pure cough syrup, my husband agreed, and it was supposed to be a fruity pineapple raspberry martini (Sonoran Martini). We got our first plate and one of the waiters or hosts followed me back to the table to asked if my husband enjoyed the football then asked if he ignored me a lot during it.. which to me was incredibly rude/crossing a boundary. We had our first round and it took until was almost done with our second plates for anyone to grab the first two empty plates on our table.. yet three wait staff said goodbye to us when we left so I know they we not understaffed at all.. then the kicker was two of the desserts ran out, our reservations were at 7:15 and we left by 8:40. How do you run out of the two out of the four desserts you’re serving and still charging folks full price? Plus it’s not like we showed up astronomically late, we were on time and it’s insane that they ran out early.. why offer a buffet when you can’t actually keep up with the intake of your guests? All together I would never recommend this to anyone, unless you want to throw away your money to the name of the Phoenician. Bad service, over priced and disappointing menu experiences.

reviews.text: My husband and I were so disappointed in our meal here. The one thing to mention that was positive is that the view of you sit outside is stellar. Unfortunately that does not make up for the rest.  Our general impression was that this is a place for hotel guests so no repeat business. When we got to the restaurant it looked to be about half full so our experience was not due to the staff or kitchen being slammed with an extra large party. We arrived at the time of our reservation. There was no one to seat us for almost 5 minutes. We did see servers walk nearby but no host or hostess anywhere to be seen.  After bringing us to a table it was about five more minutes until our server brought out water and asked for drinks. Then another ten minutes before he came to take our order. Then nearly 25 minutes before our food came which probably would not have bothered us if he had come to check on us and get us a water refill. As the sun was setting the mosquitoes came out in force and we asked if a table was available inside. We could see 2 empty tables. I am not making this up:  we watched our server clear the dishes off of one (did not wash it off or put our new napkins or cups) and then he came out to tell us to come on inside. We waited a minute to see if he would return but he did not so we brought our dishes, cups, silverware, and napkins to the table inside juggling our hands to open the door. Other diners noticed but none of the wait staff did. And about 5 minutes later we noticed another couple bringing their own meal inside too. The food was mediocre.  I had the salmon on a Caesar salad.  Not much seasoning on the salmon and not much dressing on the salad. My husband had the cowboy bison burger. It came lukewarm and the bacon was not crisp. The final straw was the live entertainment of the dueling pianos. This could have been a lot of fun. The guy had some talent but the woman sang off key and the noise level made it really hard to have a conversation.

Salad offered fresh and tasty ingredients while the sandwich was juicy and full of flavor. Sweet potato chips are an excellent side. The only disappointment - and I do hope the management reconsiders - is that cocktails that used to be (and still advertised online) as $7 during happy hour are now doubled at $14. My margarita was good but I would not purchase in the future at that extravagant happy hour price. Draft beer is still $7 and great for my spouse who enjoyed a hazy IPA. But I prefer cocktails. Please bring back the $7 special.

reviews.text: I do not recommend going here. Something has changed. We have visited here multiple times in the past and was a completely a different experience. The hostesses were a major problem. We made reservations the day before for two inside. When we arrived they sat us in the bar, which is not reserved seating it’s first come open seating, and sat us right up against exterior sliding doors which was very cold. We asked the hostess if we could have a booth or a table in the dining room, since we made reservations. She refused and said those reservations were for larger parties. She was very rude. To make things worse, I peaked in the dining room, and there were several tables with only 2 guests and half the tables were still open. Over the next 45 minutes only 2 parties were seated in the dining room, one larger party of 5 and PARTY OF 2! To make it worse, my wife ordered a hamburger, medium well, and it came out bloody, she couldn’t eat any of it. My chicken thigh dinner was overcooked and dry. The food was terrible. The only memorable portion of the night was Marvis the bartender. He made amazing drinks and offered great service. If you go, sit at the bar and GET DRINKS ONLY. reviews.text:
Overall experience was very poor. This was our first time dining at The Tavern and had high expectations given The Phoenicians reputation. We arrived at 6 for our reservation and sat for well over 10 minutes before anyone even acknowledged us.  A waiter asked us if our waiter had been to our table yet to which we replied no, they said they would send them straight over. The hostess showed up 5 minutes later, apologized for our wait and asked if she could get us a couple waters while we waited. At this point the family of four who walked in before us (and had yet to be waited on at all) got up and left. 

Eventually the original waiter came back and took our order, whoever was supposed to wait on us never showed up. We ordered fried pickles as an appetizer which took over 30 minutes. When our waiter finally did bring them out he told us “They were probably cold from sitting under the light for a while” and that he had put it another order of them for us (I will give him credit for that). 

My husband ordered a hamburger. The quality was very mediocre, especially given the price. I had the cob salad and it was enjoyable. We ordered chicken tenders, fruit and steamed vegetables for our 2 year old. They brought us raw carrots which she can’t eat as they’re a choking hazard. Had to wait another 10 minutes for steamed broccoli. The kids menu also states that children 3 and under eat for free. We didn’t know that when we made the reservation and it was a pleasant surprise. However, when the bill came we were charged for the meal and had to ask about having it removed. 

When all was said and done we were so disappointed with the whole experience. Although it’s located at the Phoenician, it overlooks the bag drop and parking garage. Not at all the grand view we were hoping for. The food was totally unimpressive and while our waiter was very kind the only way I can think to describe the service was as an absolute dumpster fire. 

Do yourself a favor and don’t do it.

reviews.text: The entrance was a bit confusing. There is a side stairway but it leads to anlcoked door behind the dueling piano space. Luckily, a staff member was around to open it. We went to the front desk and were seated promptly but it took a while to get our drink order. Once we were approached by the waitress and got our order for drinks in, it took a while to get our drinks - a beer flight, a mule and an iced tea. The restaurant was moderately crowded but not to the point where - like that night - we did not see servers walking around, attending to their tables. We got the beer flight first, then the mule just before the appetizers were served and then the iced tea came after appetizers came. When we ordered, we got the restaurant week specials. The appetizers were amazing (kale-artichoke dip, Nashville fried chicken and pork belly poutine). The main course was ok. The Wagyu tri-tips was very gristly, chewy and wasn't edible. The macaroni the accompanied it was great. We ended up asking for a new order of tri-tips to be cooked medium well and that actually came out way better. I had asked for the Cowboy Burger sauce to be on the side and it came on it. It was cooked well done and was an okay tasting Burger. The fish and chips was actually delightful. It was a bit too breaded, but it was nonetheless good. The chocolate cake was ok. The server was very nice and you can tell she really wanted to help, but there were a lot of gaps in time where we didn't see any servers. I think the price is a bit over-charged for what you're receiving. I would say that this is good if I were staying onsite or if someone wanted to go there, but not a restaurant I would go out of my way to visit again.

reviews.text: This is the dining establishment at the Phoenician Golf Club.  While it is good for that purpose it is not a destination dining spot. Many better options in the area.

reviews.text: The setting of the Phoenician is breath-taking, so a visit to any of its restaurants is a treat.  We valet-parked and, after a self-guided tour of the beautiful cactus garden, were taken to the Tavern by golf cart.  Our server, Cameron, was attentive and friendly.  We had the crab roll, salmon sandwich, and patty melt - all excellent choices.  Although we came at dusk, I would recommend getting there earlier so that the grounds can be appreciated.   (Fortunately, we've been there before.)
